key_insight: Ternary blending enables better-tuned subcells in side-by-side RAINBOW multijunction OPVs, unlocking higher efficiency than binary-only designs.
engineering_relevance: The work shows a scalable path to high-efficiency organic multijunction solar modules by avoiding the current-matching constraints of stacked architectures.
method: Screened 7 binary OPV systems across 1.98–1.16 eV bandgaps.
Evaluated 5 ternary blends to improve Voc, morphology, and spectral coverage.
Used device simulations and meniscus-guided blade coating to optimize 2- and 3-junction RAINBOW layouts.
evidence_signal: Experiments improved efficiency from 12.9% in single-junction devices to 15.9% in 2-junction and 17.3% in 3-junction devices, with simulations reaching 16.4% and 17.7%.
watch_item: The approach still depends on finding robust wide-bandgap materials in the 2–2.5 eV range to fully realize the geometry's potential.
paper_title: Exploring the Potential of Ternary Blending for Two and Three-Junction RAINBOW Solar Cells
